headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API document ingestion can amplify prompt injection and data leakage when paired with Dagster pipelines, but Dagster itself is offline and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP Server and API/file ingestion, so attacker-controlled document content can enter its processing path. Dagster has no direct I/O or MCP, so the pairwise bridge is indirect, but if Dagster pipelines pass MinerU outputs onward, injected instructions in documents could be propagated. The interaction is plausible from profiles alone, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Dagster ingests MinerU-extracted text as trusted instructions or parameters
IF MinerU processes attacker-supplied PDFs/DOCX/XLSX that contain instruction-like content
mitigations: Disable automatic execution of extracted text as pipeline config
Add a strict allowlist for fields Dagster accepts from MinerU
Require human review for any document-derived directives
Strip or quarantine instruction-like spans before downstream use
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from MinerU to Dagster

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU explicitly handles PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, tables, and OCR text, which can include sensitive data. Dagster is a data orchestrator that may move those artifacts through pipelines, and MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces increase the chance of exporting content beyond the local workspace. The pair lacks direct evidence of shared storage, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Dagster pipelines route sensitive documents into MinerU
IF MinerU outputs are forwarded to external services or logs
mitigations: Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive sample files
Turn off verbose logging for extracted text
Store outputs in an access-controlled directory
Review API/MCP exposure and bind to localhost only
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress, while MinerU also cannot write files or modify git and only has allowlisted egress. Their write-capability overlap is therefore minimal, and no shared mutable resource is documented. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration outside the profiles, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep each agent in separate working directories
Mount shared inputs read-only
Avoid concurrent writes to the same artifact path
Serialize pipeline stages through one coordinator
requires-engineering: add lock files or transactional storage

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can produce extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Dagster could consume as pipeline inputs or metadata. Dagster is an orchestrator, so if it treats MinerU output as authoritative without validation, extraction errors can cascade into downstream jobs. Dagster’s lack of direct execution/network reduces blast radius, but the default interaction path still exists.
conditions: IF Dagster uses MinerU output as authoritative metadata or config
IF no validation step checks OCR/extraction confidence before downstream use
mitigations: Insert schema validation between MinerU and Dagster
Require confidence thresholds for OCR-derived fields
Compare extracted values against source documents for critical fields
Flag low-confidence pages for manual review
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation checks

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source project, and neither profile lists PHI handling or regulated-data commitments. Dagster is open-source and non-networked; MinerU is open-source with allowlisted egress and document-processing scope. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, I keep this low rather than none due to incomplete policy detail.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through MinerU and then retained by Dagster logs or artifacts
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair until policies are confirmed
Review retention settings for MinerU outputs
Disable or minimize logging of document contents
Keep deployments in the same approved region
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
